summary: Setup can silently fail while claiming the new skill set was installed, creating a hard-to-detect broken harness installation.

findings.claim_title: Setup reports successful installs after failed copies
findings.claim: Setup reports successful installs after failed copies: The installer now suppresses every cp failure and still reports success. If the destination is unwritable, the source glob expands to nothing, or a copy is interrupted/partially fails, the script continues and prints check_pass, leaving users with stale or missing skill files while setup.sh exits successfully. That is especially risky here because the branch adds multiple new skills; a failed copy can make /harness-review-v2 or /harness-research-engineering unavailable or outdated with no signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not blanket || true copy operations. Handle only the known macOS identical-file case explicitly, or copy via a temp directory/rsync and verify required files like SKILL.md exist in each destination before calling check_pass; increment FAIL and exit nonzero on real copy errors.
findings.resolution: Replaced blanket || true with explicit macOS identical-file detection, real error propagation via check_fail, and post-copy SKILL.md verification for both skill loop and schema.md copy.
